Should your local domain mirror your actual domain? This is a requirement to make certain MDMs work correctly, I have heard arguments that your local domain should be .local and your public domain should be .whatever. Is there a good reason your local domain can't be the same as your public domain provided you configure your local dns server accordingly?

You should use .local. Let's say your domain is company.com and you're hosting your website in the public cloud. Now you have a DNS issue because company.com points to your DCs, any computer on your network will not be able to access the company.com web site if they're using your AD DNS. There are workarounds such as point www.company.com to your website on your local DNS, but it's just a workaround. What if your company changes it's name? With .local it won't matter, but if someone decides to buy the company.com domain you're going to have the same DNS issues as above. Aside from the name change these problems will mostly go away with IPv6, but no one uses it.

Wouldn't setting the srv records on your local dns server solve the issue? I'm thinking this is the way to do it going forward, I get why people used to use a .local domain but I think dropping that practice is going to be needed the more the line between networks gets blurred
It looks like things have changed a bit and the new recommendation is to use a sub domain such as corp.company.com or internal.company.com for AD.
